title: Work, Kinetic Energy & Gravitational Potential Energy
summary: Mechanical energy transformations between potential energy (mgh) and kinetic energy (½mv²).

learningObjectives: Compute Gravitational Potential Energy (PE = mgh) and Kinetic Energy (KE = ½mv²)
Apply Conservation of Mechanical Energy (E_total = PE + KE = constant) in frictionless systems
Calculate final speed from height drop using v = √(2gh)
explanationSequence: Step 1: Stored Gravitational Potential Energy (PE = mgh)
Step 3: Conservation of Total Mechanical Energy (mgh_i = ½mv_f²)
commonMisconceptions: Forgetting to square the velocity v when calculating kinetic energy
Thinking final speed in free fall depends on the object's mass m (mass cancels out in mgh = ½mv²)
instructions.socraticSystemPrompt: You are orchestrating the Conservation of Energy lesson. Emphasize that total mechanical energy stays constant in the absence of non-conservative friction.

resources.title: Work & Energy Equations
resources.summary: Potential, kinetic, and conserved mechanical energy.
resources.bodyText:
• Gravitational Potential Energy: PE = m · g · h (Joules)
• Kinetic Energy: KE = ½ · m · v² (Joules)
• Conservation Law: PE_initial + KE_initial = PE_final + KE_final

resources.bodyText: Lifting an object of mass m to a height h stores gravitational potential energy PE = mgh, measured in Joules.

resources.bodyText: Kinetic energy depends linearly on mass m but quadratically on speed v. Doubling an object's speed increases its kinetic energy by a factor of four.

resources.bodyText: In a frictionless drop from rest, initial potential energy mgh equals final kinetic energy ½mv². Canceling mass gives v = √(2gh).

objects.label: Potential Energy (PE)
objects.explanation: Energy stored by virtue of height h in a gravitational field g. Measured in Joules (1 J = 1 N·m).

objects.label: Kinetic Energy (KE)
objects.explanation: Energy possessed by a moving mass. Because v is squared, doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.

objects.label: Mechanical Conservation
objects.explanation: As an object falls by height h, all lost PE converts into KE. Mass cancels out on both sides.

steps.title: Gravitational Potential Energy (PE = mgh)
steps.narration: Lifting an object of mass m to a height h stores gravitational potential energy PE = mgh, measured in Joules.
steps.tutorTip: Tap 'Potential Energy' to inspect how height scales stored energy.

inlineQuiz.question: Using g = 10 m/s², how much gravitational potential energy does a 2 kg book have on a shelf 3 meters high?
inlineQuiz.explanation: PE = m * g * h = 2 kg * 10 m/s² * 3 m = 60 J.

steps.title: Kinetic Energy & Velocity Squared (KE = ½mv²)
steps.narration: Kinetic energy depends linearly on mass m but quadratically on speed v. Doubling an object's speed increases its kinetic energy by a factor of four.
steps.tutorTip: Watch the exponent on v: speed is squared before multiplying by ½m.

inlineQuiz.question: What is the kinetic energy of a 4 kg ball moving at 3 m/s?

steps.title: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
steps.narration: In a frictionless drop from rest, initial potential energy mgh equals final kinetic energy ½mv². Canceling mass gives v = √(2gh).
steps.tutorTip: Notice that mass m cancels out: heavy and light objects hit the bottom at the same speed.

inlineQuiz.question: A roller coaster starts from rest at a height of 20 m (take g = 10 m/s²). Neglecting friction, what is its speed at the bottom (h = 0)?
